 21-Year-Old Jung Jae-hyun Secures First Regular Tour Win at KPGA 2026 Season Finale
 Jeon Yeongmin 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.11.08 17:16 
 View 
 View Count 
 Enlarge image 
 ▲ Tour Championship Winner Jung Jae-hyun 
 Jung Jae-hyun has claimed his first regular tour victory at the KPGA Tour Championship (total prize pool of 1.1 billion KRW), the final event of the 2026 Korean Professional Golfers' Association (KPGA) tour season. 
 Playing in the final fourth round of the tournament held today (November 8) at the Valley and Teddy courses of Teddy Valley Golf & Resort (par 72) in Seogwipo, Jeju Island, Jung delivered a stellar performance by firing eight birdies without a single bogey. 
 Starting the day tied for second and one stroke behind the leader, Jung finished with a total of 13-under 275, beating runner-up Hwang Jaemin (total 10-under 278), who is approaching his 40th birthday, by a 3-stroke margin. 
 Jung's final-round score of 8-under 64 ties the course record. 
 Brandon Kawalamani (United States) and Kim Hong-taek also added their names to the course record. 
 Jung received 224.8 million KRW in prize money and boosted his Genesis points ranking to 8th, also pocketing a bonus prize of 18 million KRW. 
 Debuting on the regular tour in 2024, 21-year-old Jung had previously won twice on the secondary tour, but this marks his first regular tour title. 
 He also neatly washed away the disappointment of finishing as the runner-up in a playoff at the Lexus Masters last week. 
 Kim Min-gyu and Jeong Han-mil each carded 5-under rounds to tie for 3rd place at 9-under 279 overall. 
 Meanwhile, Shin Sang-hun, who finished in a tie for 24th place at 1-over 289, became the winner of the Genesis Grand Prix award for the first time in his career.
